source.title: Unified regularity measures for sample-wise learning and generalization
source.authors: Chi Zhang; Meng Yuan; Xiaoning Ma; Yu Liu; Hao-Ang Lu; Le Wang; Yuanqi Su; Yue-Hu Liu

record.file_problem: The supplied text is the full paper; no material cutoff or garbling affects the relevant sections.
record.tranche_reason: The study uses sample regularity measures, including CBTL and forgetting events, to select training examples and reports test accuracy after removal. It does not test the claim versions’ specified interventions or measurements.
record.gate_note: Section 4.1 reports test accuracy after removing samples selected by density, forgetting events, CBTL, or at random. Architecture and optimizer comparisons report changes in sample-distribution representations, not the generalization gaps named by the versions. Results for testing-set sampling concern evaluation-set composition and are outside the claim.
record.test_reason: Table 3 reports the study's own classification accuracies for convolutional networks and an MLP on CIFAR-10, bearing on V3. The extraction overlooks this comparison when excluding testing-set sampling results. Training protocols are insufficiently described to establish a controlled architectural comparison. The sample-removal experiments do not test V8's inclusion-based memorization criterion.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that paired training/testing regularity representations describe similar sample distributions and that high-regularity samples contribute little to their training and evaluation tasks, enabling sample reduction.
record.recipe_differences: The study applies sample-selection measures to training acceleration; it does not reproduce a claim-version method.
record.method_sensitivity: The radius used to calculate density changes training performance; the authors report relatively best overall performance at r = 1. Different optimizers produce substantially different sample-distribution representations.

fits_no_version.finding: Removing 60% of training samples using regularity-based strategies retains accuracy above 0.91; random removal degrades performance faster.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Regularity-based training-set reduction can preserve accuracy better than random removal on CIFAR-10.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 1 compares SVM predictions with and without training samples selected by synchronization of forgetting and mal-generalizing events.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Some synchronized training samples improve prediction of particular test examples using pretrained image features.

record.problems: The removal curves are presented in a figure without exact values or uncertainty estimates in the text. The reported experiment uses ResNet-110 on Cifar-10; it does not establish the claim versions’ mechanisms or generalization-gap measurements.
record.rows_left_out: No other rows retained. Section 4.1 also reports density-radius comparisons and testing-set sampling results, but these do not measure a version’s named behavior; the testing-set sampling results alter evaluation-set composition. Sections 3.3.1–3.3.2 and 3.3.3 compare sample-distribution statistics across runs, architectures, and optimizers, not the claim’s generalization gap.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and matched natural-label versus random-label held-out performance.
Width-dependent test error beyond the width required for zero training error.

Matched training protocols, training from scratch with standard gradient methods, the contribution of local connectivity, learned sparse connections, and convolutional initialization of fully connected networks are not established.
Held-out optimizer comparisons under limited or broader tuning; optimizer experiments here compare sample statistics.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Dropout interventions and their dependence on dataset size, augmentation, or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, generalization-gap correlations, and comparisons with alternative measures.
Removal and retraining based on inclusion-defined label memorization versus equally sized random removal.

missing.what: Add convolutional-versus-MLP accuracy comparisons for the original 10,000-example test set and the two 400-example subsets. Although rows_left_out dismisses evaluation-set sampling, it does not capture these architecture comparisons. Record the unspecified training protocols.

record.verdict_notes: The supplied text supports descriptive architecture comparisons, not attribution of their differences to locality. Synchronization, forgetting counts, and cumulative correct classifications are not interchangeable with V8's inclusion-based memorization measure.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label training or natural-label versus random-label held-out comparison.
No width sweep around the zero-training-error threshold.
No comparison of convolutional and fully connected networks’ test errors.
Optimizer comparisons concern sample-distribution representations, not held-out performance or generalization gaps.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurement or comparison with generalization gaps.
Examples are selected by density, forgetting events, or CBTL, not by the stated inclusion-based memorization criterion.

rows.subject: ResNet-110
rows.operation_detail: Removed training examples in descending order of density in the proposed bi-dimensional representation, then evaluated test accuracy.
rows.baseline: None (no training samples removed); figure only
rows.note: The text says accuracy remains above 0.91 after removing 60% for the sample-selection strategies collectively, and that the proposed strategy slightly outperforms CBTL and forgetting events; it does not state this strategy’s exact value.
rows.check: This evaluates the proposed selection method, not a claim version. High-density selection does not identify examples by inclusion-based memorization. The text supplies only a collective accuracy bound above 0.91 at 60% removal.

rows.subject: ResNet-110

rows.check: Forgetting-event selection does not measure V8's memorization criterion. This is a method comparator; its exact accuracy is unavailable in the supplied figure text.

relationships.condition: CIFAR-10 classifiers as evaluated in Table 3, on the original test set and both difficulty-balanced subsets.
relationships.reason: Based on text missing from the rows: all listed convolutional classifiers outperform the MLP. Original-set accuracy is 0.7353–0.9542 versus 0.4440; 10-bin accuracy is 0.3875–0.8150 versus 0.3050; 4-bin accuracy is 0.4925–0.8425 versus 0.3925. Training details do not establish a controlled architectural explanation.
relationships.display_finding: The reported higher accuracy of every listed convolutional classifier over the MLP remains unverified across the three evaluations.
